rules.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which includes both at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause as defined in the ordinance.
rules.summary_plain: Your landlord cannot evict you unless they have a legally valid reason defined as just cause under San Diego law.
rules.summary_plain_es: Su arrendador no puede desalojarlo a menos que tenga una razón legal válida definida como causa justa según la ley de San Diego.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to residential rental properties except those exempted under section 98.0703.
rules.exemptions_text: Exemptions include transient and tourist hotel occupancy, short-term residential occupancy, deed-restricted affordable housing, mobilehomes under Mobilehome Residency Law, nonprofit transitional housing, dormitories owned by educational institutions, landlord-occupied units with shared facilities, single-family residences occupied by the landlord with limited rented rooms, properties with certificate of occupancy issued within last 15 years (except mobilehomes), and certain owner-occupied properties not owned by corporations or REITs.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
